newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt shares fall in lower than average turnover.
newsitem.headline: Egypt shares fall in lower than average turnover.

text.p: Egyptian share prices fell on Thursday as the market wound down in advance of holidays in Europe and most of the rest of the world.
The Capital Market Authority (CMA) all-share index closed 0.96 points down at 286.80 on turnover of 37.31 million pounds ($11.0 million), slightly lower than average.
"It's just the close of the week, coming before the holidays," said Neveen el-Tahry of brokers Delta EAB.
Two active shares, Heliopolis Housing and Development and Helwan Portland Cement, bucked the trend because of a widespread view that they remain undervalued.
"People think Heliopolis Housing is worth much more than they originally calculated," said Tahry.
"Foreign investors have been looking at its net asset value, as they did with Medinet Nasr, and they calculate that the share price still hasn't reached it," said another broker.
The shares closed 28.00 pounds up at 428.00 in trade worth almost three million pounds.
Helwan Cement, the most active share of all, rose 0.75 pounds to end the trading week at 60.00 and Tahry said she thought it could keep rising for a while.
"It's still at a very attractive P/E ratio, it's still a good price. It has a long way to go," she said.

Four partially privatised milling firms extended their losing streak in moderate volume. All had risen sharply since privatisation earlier this year and a bout of profit taking has hit them throughout the week.
Central and West Delta Flour Mills closed 0.25 down at 81.50, East Delta Flour Mills down 2.24 at 51.25, Upper Egypt Flour Mills down 3.65 at 67.85, North Cairo Flour Mills down 0.25 at 131.00.
The CMA index for openly traded firms fell sharply to 427.17 from 433.92 on Wednesday while the index for rarely traded "closed" firms rose to 202.83 from 202.07.
From the 87 shares traded, 17 rose, 31 fell and 39 ended the day unchanged, the CMA said.
